name: End times & prophecy
about: The rapture, the day of the Lord, and Christ's reign.

teachings.title: The battle of Armageddon
teachings.summary: At Armageddon Christ defeats the beast's armies with the sword of His mouth, casting the antichrist and false prophet into the lake of fire and leaving the wicked to the fowls.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 13:9**
*Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.*

**Joel 3:12-14**
*Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about. Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.*

*Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.*

Armageddon, the "Mountain of Assembly," refers to Mt Zion. The valley of Jehoshaphat, the valley of judgment, is the space between Zion and Mt Olive, where Christ will rule during the Millennial Reign.

It is here the armies of the beast assemble and ride out to battle Jesus,
King Of Kings, And Lord Of Lords.

*And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.*

The antichrist and his false prophet are instantly cast into the lake of fire. The remnant of their armies slain by the sword that comes from the mouth of Christ. The two-edged sword, which immediately calls to mind the word of God. Spoken from Jesus mouth, with the power to slay the wicked, leaving their carcasses for the carrion birds to feed on.

**Jeremiah 7:33**
*And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.*

**Ezekiel 39:17**
*And, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood.*

teachings.title: The burden of Babylon and the day of His wrath
teachings.summary: Isaiah's prophecy against Babylon has a dual fulfillment, in the fall of the Babylonian empire and in the destruction of the spirit of Babylon in the wrath to come, when no silver or gold can deliver.
teachings.text:
The prophecy of Isaiah against Babylon, they the day of the Lord is at hand, clearly has dual fulfillment. It speaks not only of the destruction of Babylonian empire, which had only risen to prominence in the days of Isaiah, but that same spirit of Babylon which will be destroyed in the wrath to come.

...*cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it. For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine. And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.*

**Malachi 3:2**
*But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?*

And as Isaiah preached, the Persians and Medes had no regard for gold and silver, the Lord's judgment can't be swayed either.

**Zephaniah 1:18**
*Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord's wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.*

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

teachings.title: Psalm 7 and the day of the Lord
teachings.summary: Psalm 7 prophesies the day of the Lord, when after the tribulation Christ returns and the resurrected and living saints are caught up to compass Him about in the air before the wrath.
teachings.text:
**Psalms 7:6–9**
*Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me to the judgment that thou hast commanded. So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about: for their sakes therefore return thou on high. The LORD shall judge the people: judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity that is in me. Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end; but establish the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.*

This passage in **Psalms 7** is prophetic to the day of the Lord, Jesus' second coming, the rapture and the wrath.

The congregation of the people, the resurrection of the saints, gathered together in the air to meet Him at His glorious coming.

**Matthew 24:27–31**
*For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together. Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

As eagles, carrion birds, circle a carcass, so will the risen saints "compass about" Jesus, as we meet Him in the air. When He returns with His own, the spirits of the dead, raising them first, and then those which are alive and remain:

**1 Thessalonians 4:14–17**
*For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep. For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

David looked forward to this day of judgement, the day of the Lord. The day of redemption.

teachings.title: Christ the King of all the earth
teachings.summary: Psalm 47 prophesies Jesus, who is God, ascending with a shout and returning with a trumpet to catch up the saints, reign as King of kings over every nation, and finally deliver the kingdom to the Father.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 47** is a song of praise for the Lord, the King of kings. Christ Jesus, Who shall put every nation under His feet.

**Revelation 11:15–17**
*And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever. And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O LORD God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.*

He shall rule and reign with a rod of iron, and give to all His people their inheritance in His Kingdom.

Jesus is God. Verse 5 says *God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.* A prophetic Old Testament verse, made clear in the New Testament, carrying the comfort of all believers;

**1 Thessalonians 4:16–17**
*For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

We shall sing of the glories of the Lord, forever.

**Revelation 7:10–12**
*And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen.*

**Revelation 19:16**
*And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.*

For Jesus is the King of all the earth, and reigns over the heathen. All the nations. He is greatly exalted above every name.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus will reign over all things, and, having defeated death and been made ruler of all, He will give all to God the Father. A perfect sacrifice, holy and acceptable, made holy by His righteousness:

**1 Corinthians 15:24–27**
*Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him*.

**Psalm 47** is a wonderful and prophetic song of praise and worship for the Kingdom of God, under our Lord Christ Jesus. All honor and praise is His. Amen

teachings.title: Gather my saints together unto me
teachings.summary: Psalm 50, a prophecy of Asaph the seer in God's own voice, shows Christ the Creator returning in fire to judge, and the gathering of His saints before His wrath is poured out, proving the rapture is no new doctrine.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 50**, is a song written directly from the voice of God to His people, His own perspective directly to man. It is instruction in doctrine and prophecy, by His word. In the first person.

He spoke these things through a psalmist other than David. The superscript titles this as "A Psalm of Asaph," making it the very first of the 12 "Asaphite Psalms" in the Bible.

Asaph was a prominent Levite, appointed by King David as the chief musician and worship leader before the Ark of the Covenant when it was brought to Jerusalem. More than just a song director, the Bible credits him as a prophet. A seer.

**2 Chronicles 29:30**
*Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the LORD with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.*

While prophesying may refer to preaching the word of God, seer is the specific term for a visionary who is given glimpses of the future by God, prophetic understanding of things that are not but will be.

He begins his song by introducing its Author. The mighty God. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, it is God breathed, and spoken. But this will be the word of God, as a message of judgment for His people.

It establishes first the primacy of God, the Creator. By His Word the earth and the heavens were made.

**John 1:1–4**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men.*

It is important when we see credit for creation to God in the Bible, to remember that this includes Jesus.

**1 Corinthians 8:6**
*But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.*

We have a New Testament understanding when we reflect on the Old Testament revelations. The nature of the Godhead is revealed in the creation. And it is relevant to this Psalm.

Out of Zion, the place God chose to put His name, God hath shined.

His presence in the Tabernacle and the eventual Temple, God with His people through their worship, is an echo to the true coming of the Lord in the flesh, and His return on His day to judge the nations, upon that holy mountain.

*Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous round about him.*

The Second Coming, the return of Christ, is the day we all look forward to with gladness. He will come with power, a consuming fire proceeding from Him, and the sword of His word from His mouth shall slay the wicked.

**2 Thessalonians 1:7–9**
*And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power*

The future judgment of the world was a key part of the Israelites understanding, though through a glass darkly. However, having the full revelation of the complete Bible, we see clearly what they only glimpsed in faith.

He comes as a judge, the Son calling up to Heaven, and down to Earth, with a shout, with trumpet, the call to judgment of His people, before His wrath is poured out on the world.

*Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice. And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge himself. Selah.*

The gathering of the elect, those sanctified by the Spirit in Christ, is not a "new doctrine," as some would claim. The Rapture, or the gathering of the elect being caught up together to meet the Lord in the air, was a key part of prophecy for the Lord's people.

teachings.title: To Him did all prophets give witness
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: Isaiah 66, quoted throughout the New Testament, encapsulates the believer's hope of a new heaven and earth, Christ's judgment of the wicked, and rest for those who trust Him.
teachings.text:
I'm running late and I will come back to this but in the meantime here are a list of New Testament verses that directly quote or allude to **Isaiah 66**:

**Acts 7:49-50**

**Matthew 5:34-35**

**2 Thessalonians 1:7-8**

**Revelation 19:11-15**

**2 Peter 3:13**

**Revelation 21:1**

**Mark 9:42-48**

A new Heaven and a new Earth, Jesus having the Earth as His footstool. Slaying with the sword that proceedeth out of His mouth. And fiery flame of judgment. And those who trust in Him entering into His rest.

The final chapter of Isaiah, like the final book of the Bible, the Revelation of Jesus, perfectly encapsulates the hope that we have set before us.

To Him did all prophets give witness.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple as what could have been
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple may be read as what could have been, since God with foreknowledge set conditional promises before Israel under the Mosaic covenant, which they failed to keep.
teachings.text:
Here in **Ezekiel 45**, the instructions for a temple and a time where there will be a priesthood of Zadok, Levites given land by cast lots for suburbs around the restored Temple. And sacrifices made for various offerings, the measure of which are given for "just balances," precise volumes, that nothing is cheated or anyone give more than another.

Similar to the existing Levitical laws, given unto Moses, the prophesied Temple in **Ezekiel 40-48** has similar Old Testament offerings and carnal ordinances, Sabbaths and holy days, done away with in the reformation of the New Testament.

We have looked at 4 main theories regarding this prophecy.; that it is symbolic and represents the church in Christ and Jesus our temple.

That it is literal, meant to be the design for the 2nd Temple Ezra will begin after captivity. That they fell short in grandeur and size.

That it is a future Temple, for the 3rd Temple leading up to the beginning of the Tribulation.

That it is a Temple in the millennial Kingdom, or in the eternal Kingdom.

All these theories have problems that make them more and more unlikely to be true. The secret things are His and we see through a glass darkly, but surely there's a purpose and a reason for Ezekiel to cap off his end times prophecies, that extend back to chapter 33. That the restoration promised also applies to the prophecy of the Temple.

Which brings us to another theory which I truthfully hadn't considered before. The interpretation of "what could have been."

First, we must acknowledge that God knows the end from the beginning, and the invisible things of what hasn't happened yet.

**Isaiah 46:9-10**
*Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.*

God knows our decisions before we make them, but also allows us the free will to make them, and gives constant appeals to repentance, and encourages us to choose His ways and seek His paths.

The Lord gave the covenant to Israel through Moses with this clear understanding.

**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it. But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

God made these conditional promises to Israel as a nation, with the foreknowledge that they would fail. Unlike the Abrahamic and Davidic covenants, which were mostly unconditional (depending on the men themselves to believe God, and have it counted for righteousness), the Mosaic covenant, with the commandments and Levitical laws, depended on the people to keep up their end in order to obtain the Kingdom and the promises and the blessings that would come if they would. And in His grace, multiple opportunities for restitution if they failed.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple: a promise on condition
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: The temple vision was a conditional promise to Israel of Christ and a kingdom if they repented, which they refused, as Christ lamented over Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
Ezekiel is no different. It is the explicit purpose of the Temple prophecy, giving the people a promise, contingent on their getting right:

**Ezekiel 43:10-11** 
*Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them*.

The promises given the people included Christ, and a Kingdom, if they repented towards the Law and God.

**Zachariah 6:12-15**
*Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is* The Branch*; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the Lord. And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the Lord, and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God.*

They could be children of the Kingdom if they were ashamed of their abominations, took the chastening God consistently gave them, and like the heathen of Nineveh, turned from the wicked ways,

God sent prophets, and they killed them. God wiped out the Northern Kingdom as an example. He brings Judah into bondage under Babylon, and makes His holy city desolate. All to goad them to come to repentance that they would be His people, and He would be their God.

**Matthew 23:37**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

teachings.title: Not by might, but by my Spirit
teachings.summary: Zechariah's golden candlestick fed by two olive trees shows that the temple is restored by God's Spirit, with lamp oil picturing the Holy Ghost, the olive trees the two witnesses of Revelation, and the candlesticks the churches.
teachings.text:
We are in **Zechariah 4** and the prophet is visited by an angel and a vision, as out of a deep sleep. He sees a golden candle stick with 7 candles, fed by oil from a bowl, with pipes from 2 olive trees beside it. Confused the prophet asks what it is he is being shown.

This is pictured in the instructions for the Tabernacle;

**Exodus 25:31-37**
*And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same. And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side: Three bowls made like unto almonds, with a knop and a flower in one branch; and three bowls made like almonds in the other branch, with a knop and a flower: so in the six branches that come out of the candlestick. And in the candlesticks shall be four bowls made like unto almonds, with their knops and their flowers. And there shall be a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick. Their knops and their branches shall be of the same: all it shall be one beaten work of pure gold. And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof: and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may give light over against it.*

**Exodus 27:20-21**
*And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always. In the tabernacle of the congregation without the vail, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the Lord: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.*

In the Bible, such as the Parable of the Ten Virgins (**Matthew 25**), lamp oil is a symbol of the Holy Spirit and spiritual preparedness. Here it is the same, the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, that it is by God's Spirit he shall restore the temple and Jerusalem.

The candles are described as being fed continuously by the two olive trees, so filled with oil they pipe it out to fill the bowls directly from their branches. Without a press and refinement. Pure.

In Revelation we learn that the two olive trees that are before the Lord, are the two witnesses. Two great men of God who give prophecy, by the word of God.

There are theories as to who these two men are. Many say Moses and Elijah, those who stood glorified with Christ on the mount of transfiguration. Others believe Elijah and Enoch, both taken up into Heaven, translated without death.

But it would make sense that either way, the continuous light of God's word, fed with the oil of His Spirit, would be upon the rebuilding of the Temple. Where Zerubbabel had laid a foundation but hadn't completed it yet.

The candles themselves represent the Spirit of God upon churches. Upon the house of God.

**Revelation 1:18-20**
*I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death. Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

The 7 candles are also tied to the 7 Spirits of the Lord;

**Revelation 1:4**
*John to the seven churches which are in Asia: Grace be unto you, and peace, from him which is, and which was, and which is to come; and from the seven Spirits which are before his throne;*

**Isaiah 11:2**
*And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord*

teachings.title: Remember thy Creator before it is too late
teachings.summary: Solomon's conclusion that all is vanity calls men to remember their Creator now, before death or the darkened sun of the day of the Lord, when it will be too late to fear Him.
teachings.text:
The end of Solomon's sermon, the preacher has spoken. Life is vanity and vexation of spirit, man toils and dies. There is iniquity and wickedness. Time and chance. A time for every purpose under Heaven. No guarantee of tomorrow. Only fleeting moments of joy where God has blessed us to enjoy the fruits of our labor. We should rejoice in our youth and remember the darkness, reflecting in mourning more than reveling in mirth. We should seek wisdom and reject foolishness, and in all things remember that there is a God, and He is just in His judgment.

And so, Solomon the king and preacher, with his thousands of proverbs, songs and sayings (and wives), sums up the end of the matter. Remember thy Creator. Remember Him in your youth, while it is still light. Before the darkness of this life or the time to come, when it is too late and tribulations and tragedies bring grief and sorrow. Before you die, and it's too late.

Before the day of the Lord.

The sun and the moon and the stars darkening is always a sign of the end, and the 2nd coming of Christ.

**Matthew 24:29-32**
*Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

**Joel 2:31**
*The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come.*

There is a time it is too late to fear the Lord, to get right with Him, to remember our Creator.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

The day of the Lord will see the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men bow, every knee shall bow and tongue confess. The rich men and rulers will beg the rocks and mountains to fall upon them. They shall have their fear come upon them. The music will cease. The streets full of mourning.

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

The grinders shall cease, for there are few...

**Matthew 24:41-42**
*Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left. Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.*

The day of our death or the day of the Lord, the end comes for all men.

*Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern*.

If our bodies are broken, our spine snapped, our skull cracked, our heart stops and we bleed out, if our body can no longer move...And ever the curse of Adam is upon us;

*Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.*

**Genesis 3:19**
*In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

...All things considered, this is the ultimate vanity. *Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.*

The preacher is wise. The wisest man in history, filled with the Spirit of God to know things and the time and treasure to consider all the ways of man under the Sun. He sought understanding and set in order many proverbs, and taught the people knowledge. Seeking truth. Instruction in uprightness. Righteousness.

*The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.*

teachings.title: Counted as sheep for the slaughter
teachings.summary: The lament of Psalm 44 is turned into instruction in Romans 8 that nothing can separate us from Christ's love, and believers grown weak by comfort must be prepared to endure persecution, even the coming tribulation, without losing faith.
teachings.text:
**1 Peter 4:12–14**
*Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy. If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.*

If the people who call themselves by His name we're naturally like Stephen, standing up for the faith and being willing to suffer death for the truth while forgiving those that stoned him to death, the New Testament wouldn't be so full of warnings and encouragement.

In **Psalm 44:22–24** they cry out desperately to God;
*Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter. Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever. Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?*

The same lament is turned to edifying instruction in the New Testament;

**Romans 8:35–37**
*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

Because man is naturally going to complain in the best of times, we need to be prepared for the proper attitude in the worst. To be persuaded that nothing can separate us from the love of Christ. Even when things are bleak.

Jesus Himself gave this encouragement to the church in Smyrna, who were facing real persecution at the hands of their enemies.

**Revelation 2:8–11**
*And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive; I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.*

Just as the instructions to live separated lives, to be holy as He is holy, is necessary because man does not by his fleshly nature do good works, even those who are saved, the same flesh tends to need reminders of past victory, while still may cry out "Why?" to their Saviour.

Righteous Job did. The best man of his generation, and yet he sought answers from God, and sinned not with his mouth while doing so, according to scripture.

Modern American Christians, made weak by the comforts and bounty God has graciously given our nation, grown fat off His blessings, will most assuredly cry out the same laments when the abomination of desolation is rolled out, and the armies of the beast strike us down.

Even the spirits of the martyrs in Great Tribulation will cry out, impatiently.

**Revelation 6:9–10**
*And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?*

We naturally may feel abandoned in the thick of it. Crying out, as the congregation does, is sadly expected.

*Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever. Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?*

We may be beaten down, bowed to the dust, despondent.
